step1.title: Welcome to Merlin!
step1.body: A quick tour of the most important features.

step2.title: Add Articles
step2.body: Tap + to save any URL, or share links from your browser, messenger app, and other apps via the Share dialog.

step3.title: Navigation Menu
step3.body: Swipe from the left edge to filter articles, browse tags, and open Settings.

step4.title: Switch View
step4.body: Prefer a compact list or visual cards? Toggle between List and Card View anytime from the navigation menu.

step5.title: Quick Actions
step5.body: Swipe any article to the left to archive it, mark it as a favorite, or delete it.

step6.title: Share Articles
step6.body: Swipe right on any article to quickly share it with friends or send it to another app.

step7.title: Reader Menu
step7.body: Swipe from the right edge while reading to share, edit article tags, set reminders, and more.

step8.title: Appearance
step8.body: Customize font, size, theme, and line spacing to match your reading preference.

step9.title: Tags
step9.body: Organize your reading list with tags. Add or remove them any time from the reader menu.

step10.title: Reminders
step10.body: Set a reminder so you don't forget to read an article. Find all reminders in the navigation menu.

step11.title: Report Articles
step11.body: Found broken formatting? Report the article so we can fix that.

step12.title: Highlights
step12.body: Select any text while reading to highlight it in one of five colors. Highlights are synced with your account.

step13.title: Shake to Undo
step13.body: Archived or deleted something by accident? Just shake your phone to undo your last action.

sampleArticle.title: Otters could become native to Berlin again
sampleArticle.byline: By Julian von Bülow · rbb|24 · 8 min · May 2026
sampleArticle.body: Poor water quality and densely built riverbanks: otters were long considered extinct in Berlin. Since the 1960s they've been under strict protection, and since the 1990s their numbers have been rising again. In the 18th and 19th centuries they were heavily hunted, seen as competitors for food and prized for their fur. In recent years, thanks to wildlife and nature conservation, their population has recovered and they've increasingly been spotted in eastern Berlin. The modern urban environment, however, still poses many dangers for otters.

settingsPreview.demoTitle: The quiet craft of reading well
settingsPreview.demoParagraph1: In an age of infinite feeds, the act of finishing an article has quietly become a small rebellion. Saving something to read later is a wager — that this version of you, the calmer one, will return to it.
settingsPreview.demoParagraph2: Most never do. The list grows; guilt accrues. The trick, it turns out, isn't discipline. It's design: a place that doesn't shout, type that breathes, a margin wide enough to think in.
settingsPreview.demoParagraph3: Set your column to a comfortable measure — somewhere between sixty and seventy-five characters. Choose a face you trust. The rest is just sitting still.
